subject: Clarification on Redwood default retention: requests, prompts, outputs and residency
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@evergreenbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <procurement@evergreenbank.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on default retention / residency for trial POC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Evergreen is keen to move our POC forward but security asked for a short Q&A on default retention behavior before we sign the SOW. A few items they asked me to clarify with you:

1) What is Redwood's default retention window for:
   - raw requests (full user prompts/payloads)
   - model responses / generated outputs
   - streamed fragments (partial tokens while streaming)
2) Does retention differ depending on deployment region (US vs EU)? How do you ensure data residency for a tenant pinned to EU region?
3) If we request erasure for a single user/session, what is the delivery timeline and what evidence do you provide?

If you have a one-pager or short matrix, that would be ideal. Can you also include any SOC2 evidence snippets we can show the security team?

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Information Security
Evergreen Bank

[attachment: evergreen_poc_scope.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <procurement@evergreenbank.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for trial POC

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's default behaviors and the erase path; I attached a compact matrix for your security team. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through examples.

Summary (defaults for Redwood hosted API):
- Raw requests / prompts: retained by default for 60 days. These are kept to support debugging, QA, and customer support investigations. We mark requests with tenant metadata for residency.
- Model responses / generated outputs: retained by default for 180 days. Outputs are used for quality monitoring and regression detection unless a customer opts into strict ephemeral configuration.
- Streamed fragments (intermediate token buffers): retained for up to 7 days and then purged automatically; fragments are not indexed for long-term analytics.

Residency and region behavior:
- When a customer selects EU residency at signup, all primary request/response records are stored in EU data stores and backups are geo‑fenced to EU buckets.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments (Reserved or VPC), customers can require on‑prem or customer-controlled storage; in those cases Redwood's control plane will honor the residency flags and provide audit logs.

Erasure process and SLAs:
- Customer-initiated erasure request (single user/session): intake -> validation -> deletion run (steps below). We aim to complete validated erasure requests within 30 calendar days.
- Evidence: we provide a deletion certificate (timestamped) and a short runbook extract that lists the affected object ids and storage shards. For regulatory audits we can also provide redacted S3 purge logs (redacted to remove other tenants).

Practical notes / exceptions:
- Aggregated telemetry used for platform health (metrics/aggregate counters) is kept indefinitely in anonymized form; it contains no PII and cannot be used to reconstruct individual prompts or outputs.
- Backups: we have a standard backup retention of 90 days for hosted control-plane metadata; customer content backups follow your selected residency and retention window.
- If you require a shorter retention for the POC (e.g., prompts removed after 0 days), we can enable an ephemeral flag for the project and confirm the configuration in the SOW.

Attached: retention_policy_matrix.xlsx (high-level table you can paste into your Security pack) and SOC2_section5_excerpt.pdf (relevant excerpt on data disposal controls).

Next steps:
- If this aligns, we can draft the SOW clause for a 30-day erasure SLA and EU data residency. If you'd like, I can set up a 30-minute call with Rishi (security ops) and Marissa (product compliance) to finalize wording.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[attachment: retention_policy_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@evergreenbank.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for trial POC

Kimberly — quick clarifying points to share with legal/security:

- Deletion evidence: we will include the shard ids and UTC timestamps in the certificate; we should avoid including raw object keys that could expose other tenants.
- For the POC we can offer a 30-day default for both prompts and outputs (temporary override) if Evergreen needs a tighter window; this is a config flag on the tenant profile.

Elena — can you confirm whether Evergreen needs:
  a) EU residency + 30-day retention for the POC, or
  b) US residency + our default (60/180/7) retention?

I'll be on the call if you pick (a) and want us to walk the runbook.

— Rishi
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@evergreenbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <procurement@evergreenbank.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-27T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for trial POC

Thanks — that helps a lot. For the POC Evergreen will choose (a): EU residency + 30-day retention for prompts and outputs.

Can we schedule the call for Monday 2027-05-03 at 10:00 CET to confirm the SOW language and the erasure certificate format? Also, please include a short paragraph we can copy into our security attestation about how backups and logs are handled during erasure.

Samir — please confirm procurement availability; we want the POC to start the week after.

Best,
Elena
